Combative

/kum-BAT-iv/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Combative means eager or ready to fight, argue, or resist.

The panelist turned combative in the first five minutes, interrupting every answer with a challenge.

Worked Example

The budget hearing was supposed to be routine. Instead, the new council member contested the very first line item, demanded the treasurer defend a decade-old decision, and challenged the chair's right to limit her speaking time — twice. When a colleague offered a compromise, she called it surrender. Observers agreed the council had gained its most combative member in memory.

Contesting every item, challenging the chair, and treating compromise as surrender show someone actively spoiling for a fight — the eagerness to battle that combative names.

How Combative Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

belligerent

belligerent: openly hostile and aggressive - in formal use, actually waging war; combative is about a person's argument-picking, fight-seeking manner

quarrelsome

quarrelsome: prone to picking arguments

Antonyms

peaceable

peaceable: inclined to avoid conflict

conciliatory

conciliatory: seeking to soothe and reconcile

How Strong Is It? — assertive → combative → warlike

assertive vs. combative

assertive vs. combative: Assertive is weaker than combative: an assertive person states positions firmly but fairly, while a combative one turns every exchange into a fight.

warlike vs. combative

warlike vs. combative: Warlike is stronger than combative — warlike suggests readiness for open, organized battle, while combative describes a person's argumentative, fight-seeking manner.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of combative.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — com-

Prefix — com-: with; against one another

Root — bat

Root — bat: to beat, strike (Latin battuere)

Suffix — -ive

Suffix — -ive: tending to; having the nature of

Put it together

Put it together: Combative is the unit pattern with its fists up: com- ('with, against one another') + bat ('to beat, strike' — the root of batter and battery) + -ive ('inclined to'). Combat is literally 'striking against one another,' and combative means 'characterized by readiness to strike' — in modern use, usually with words rather than fists.

Use the root in a new word: batter

Use the root in a new word: batter: A boxer batters an opponent with repeated blows — battuere, 'to beat,' the same striking root that arms combative with its readiness to fight.
